s.note: Cheddar twists. Cheryl calls every card without looking
s.how: Heat the oven to 200C and line two trays. Brush the pastry with egg, scatter the cheddar, parmesan and paprika over half of each sheet, fold over and press down. Cut into 1.5cm strips, twist each one, lay on the trays and sprinkle with the salt. Bake until puffed and deep golden. Cool on the trays so they crisp.

s.note: Cheddar and capsicum, crackers. The bridge is out
s.how: Beat the cream cheese and mayonnaise until smooth. Fold in the cheddar, capsicum, cayenne and lemon juice. Cover and chill to firm up. Serve in a bowl with the crackers and celery batons.

m.n: Cellar trapdoor beef and bean stew
m.note: Beef chuck slow-braised with smoky bacon, white beans, carrot and thyme, with crusty bread
m.how: Fry the bacon in the oil in a heavy pot until crisp, then lift out. Toss 900g beef in the flour and brown in batches in the bacon fat. Soften the onion, carrots, celery and garlic in the same pot. Stir in the tomato paste, then add 750ml beef stock, the thyme, bay, salt, pepper, bacon and beef. Cover and simmer on low. Add the beans and simmer uncovered until thick. Serve in bowls with torn crusty bread.

w.note: Dark cocoa, fudge icing. Ash throws the book in the fire
w.how: Heat the oven to 180C and grease and line two 20cm cake tins. Whisk the flour, cocoa, sugar, bicarb and salt in a big bowl. Whisk the eggs, buttermilk, oil and vanilla, stir into the dry mix, then whisk in the hot coffee to a thin batter. Divide between the tins and bake until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely. Heat the cream until steaming, pour over the chocolate and butter and stir until glossy, then cool until thick enough to spread. Sandwich the layers and cover the cake with the icing.

d.note: Whisky, honey, lemon. Cheryl hears a voice: join us
d.how: Push 3 cloves into each lemon round. Divide the honey, lemon juice and whisky between 4 heatproof mugs. Top with the boiling water, stir, add a studded lemon round and a cinnamon stick and leave to steep for a few minutes.
